competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

U.S. rates are mixed: SOFR is 3.88%, the 10-year is 5.12% after a modest daily dip tied to soft housing, yet the policy debate still allows for more tightening. Treasury supply continues to lean on selective buyers with yields recently at multi-decade highs. Euro-area stress shows in a 5% French 10-year; UK CPI at 3.5% keeps hike talk alive while the ECB sounds in no hurry. Risk assets are resilient—S&P 7712, Nasdaq 26425, gold 4142—with credit headlines around CoreWeave and AI capex adding an inflation undertone. BoJ follow-through supports a call-rate path near 1.25% from late September. Australian labor, inflation, retail, spending, confidence and domestic-demand releases could not be verified, so new Australian risk stays closed; New Zealand new risk is also closed.

dollar-king.thesis: United States yields still do the dollar's work: the two-year at 4.79, the ten-year at 5.12, and a SOFR strip that sits above the 3.88 fixing through next year. That is not a dollar-collapse tape, and the clean way to own it remains dollar spot rather than a cross. Dollar-Canada is the sleeve already on, but the Canadian leg has changed: crude is in three digits and Canada's relative impulse has turned higher, which is the mix that paid the loonie from the peak and gave back most of the win. The rate gap still supports a smaller long, not a full-size hold and not a fresh thirty-five million from flat.
dollar-king.invalidation: The residual long is wrong if United States two-year yields lose their premium while oil stays in three digits and Canada's relative impulse remains higher, or if dollar-Canada trades back through the original entry area near 1.401 on that mix. Unknowns: intervention, Canadian policy reaction, and the next oil impulse; no stop or target is invented here.

performance_reflections.what_happened_vs_expected: The expected path was a grind higher in dollar-Canada while United States yields stayed restrictive versus Canada. The realized path was an overshoot to a large peak, then a giveback as oil held above 100 and Canada's relative impulse improved. Residual profit is still positive versus entry but far below the maximum favorable excursion, which is a harvest failure rather than a thesis reversal on the dollar leg.
performance_reflections.lesson: After a material dollar-Canada win, three-digit oil plus a rising Canadian impulse is a harvest trigger. Remaining United States rate edge belongs in reduced size, not in a full-size hold that waits to recapture the peak.

causal.original_belief: United States rate and growth premium versus a soft Canada would keep dollar-Canada trending higher, with restrictive United States policy dominating oil and local Canadian data, so the long could be held through noise after a good entry near 1.401.
causal.observed_reality: The pair did pay to a large peak, then gave most of that open profit back as oil held in three digits and Canada's relative impulse turned higher while United States two-year and ten-year yields remained 4.79 and 5.12.
causal.assumptions_right: The United States coupon curve stayed high, the SOFR strip still prices above the 3.88 fixing, and the dollar did not collapse versus other majors. Direction versus Canada was right enough to produce a large peak and leave the book still green versus entry.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Three-digit crude and a rising Canadian relative impulse were treated as secondary overlays on a rates short of Canada. They are first-order for the Canadian leg. Harvest discipline on a material winner was underweighted versus letting the original dollar story run after the peak.
causal.causal_divergence: The peak-to-now giveback is a Canadian-leg squeeze from oil and a better Canadian impulse, not a bust of the United States rate story. Holding full size after that mix showed up converted a paid winner into a large giveback without a new dollar-negative catalyst.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same three-digit oil and the same rising Canadian factor visible into the peak, a harvest cut into strength would have locked most of the peak and left a runner. Same information, smaller size after those Canadian positives printed, would have avoided the bulk of the giveback.
causal.future_implication: Dollar-Canada size has to be conditioned on oil and the Canadian impulse. A still-valid United States rate view is not a license to hold full size in a commodity currency after a material win has already paid.

cross-merchant.thesis: The freeze still prints a Canada-versus-Japan gap that a dollar pair would smear. CADJPY is 112.54 on 20 Oct against a 110.9 entry, book mark about 112.44; WTI is 101.79 and Brent is 108.79; Canada Prima-pressure is rising with end-2027 Brent 16.58 above the July MPR 70 conditioning; CORRA is 2.26 versus March 2027 2.995; TONA is 1.227 with March 2027 TONA 1.6825; Canada 10Y is 3.93 versus Japan 10Y 2.927. That is still oil-exporter versus oil-importer, a 103bp cash-carry lead, and a BoC path that prices 73bp of tightening against 46bp in TONA, without feeding SOFR 3.88 or the 3.75-4.00 funds range through USDCAD or USDJPY. This seat reads remaining edge at the freeze: CADJPY is only the 28th one-year percentile and z -0.59, so 112.54 has not used up the cheapness that 110.9 bought, while the five-year 81st percentile is the longer-window caution, not a reason to switch expression. EURCAD at 1.5758 (2nd one-year percentile, one-month -2.07%) is CAD already having won versus the euro; chasing short EURCAD from here is a completed move, not a cleaner CA-EA differential. EURJPY at 177.34 (about the 6th one-year percentile, three-month -4.77%) is broad yen strength that CADJPY has already damped (three-month only -3.11%) because oil and carry offset Japan; long EURJPY would throw away that Canada leg. EURGBP at 0.8403 (0.2 one-year percentile) is a UK/BoE 3.75% 6-3 hold with three members preferring a hike, not an eligible US/CA/EA/JP cross and not a substitute for the CA-JP oil-policy stack. AONIA 4.60 versus CORRA 2.26 is the same known Australia-Canada cash wedge, not a new AU-versus-CA policy, growth, inflation, or carry shock, so the closed AUDCAD fade stays shut and no new Australia risk is opened. What the freeze does not show is the next BoJ/MoF yen action or whether crude stays bid; those sit in invalidation rather than in a new cross.
cross-merchant.invalidation: The Canada-Japan relative-value case fails if CADJPY gives back the post-entry advance through 110.9 alongside a reversal in WTI 101.79 and/or Brent 108.79 and/or compression of the Canada-Japan 10Y gap (3.93 versus 2.927), or if BoJ/MoF yen action reprices JPY independently of the Canadian oil, carry, and hike-path differential. causal.future_implication: When a SOFR contract lags a documented sovereign-yield backup, treat it as an expression problem and rotate to the confirming tenor instead of averaging or holding the laggard.
